nodes.label: Baseline score (skill overlap 0.6 + TF-IDF 0.4)
nodes.rationale: Only qualifications are read; names, contacts, employers, schools and dates never reach the score. Nothing to score raises an error so a failed parse does not look like a poor candidate.

nodes.label: sensitive_noise fields
nodes.rationale: About 15% of CVs print date of birth and nationality so tests can check the parser does not extract them and the scorer never sees them.

nodes.label: ESCO matching results (e5-small)
nodes.rationale: Embedding threshold 0.9 gives 46% embedding coverage but many wrong matches (Docker to dock operations, HTML to JavaScript).

nodes.label: ESCO matching results (MiniLM)
nodes.rationale: Embedding threshold 0.7 gives 41% coverage; fails on non-English inputs and short acronyms.

nodes.label: Model comparison results
nodes.rationale: MiniLM is ~3x faster (30.7 ms vs 85.9 ms per CV) but cuts 54% of CVs short at 256 tokens and is weaker cross-lingually; e5-small has higher nDCG@10 (0.906 vs 0.855).
